message.content:
Carabiners of aluminum: CBP rulings on climbing carabiners have classified them in 7616.99 (other articles of aluminum), or in 8308.90 (clasps... of base metal)? Known rulings: Black Diamond carabiners classified under 8308.90.9000 as "other clasps"? I recall NY rulings classifying carabiners in 8308.90.6000 ("Other: Other"). Actually, HTS 8308.90: 8308.90.30 is of iron or steel, 8308.90.60 is other (of base metal, including aluminum), though it was reorganized: 8308.90.3000 "Other: Of iron or steel", 8308.90.6000 "Other". Carabiners are snap hooks; heading 8308 covers "hooks, eyelets... clasps, buckles". Another view is that snap hooks are covered under 7616 for aluminum. However, I recall rulings on Petzl carabiners as 8308.90.6000, and the 2022 ruling about "Ceros" likely does the same. Going with 8308.90.6000.

{"hts_code": "8308.90.6000", "reason": "Aluminum locking carabiners are snap-hook style clasps/fasteners of base metal, classified in heading 8308 as other (not of iron or steel) under 8308.90.60."}
